status: Declared BEFORE any C feature was computed. stage_c_features refuses to run unless the features it produces are exactly this list; its hash goes into the research ledger before anything is computed. Any change after the first run is a new family.
question: Do features the library lacks - overnight/intraday decomposition, market-model residuals, lottery and liquidity measures, NSE price-band state, relative position to indicators, interactions - make stage D's model pick a better daily top-3?
inputs_allowed: the raw daily cache (open, high, low, close, volume) of each panel symbol; universe membership = panel rows; six panel feature columns for interactions: INDIAVIX_ret_1d, MKT_D_drawdown_252, D_dist_from_52wh, X_turnover_med, D_mdi14_diff1, D_WQ_44. Nothing starting label_ is ever read.
point_in_time: every per-symbol feature uses bars up to and including T only; market series and per-date ranks use only stocks in the universe on T; all verified by recomputing on data cut at T (tests) and by a future-return leak screen on the real data (stage_c_screen)
screen_rule: stage B's rule on the C features alone, as their own family: per-day Spearman IC, Newey-West t (lag 20), BH q <= 0.10 across all C cells of the 4 targets, sign in >= 4 of 5 folds, research rows only, eligible rows only. Market-level columns (group I) are described, not screened.
leak_stops: if any C feature has |IC| >= 0.15 against a target or against label_gap1 (the overnight gap it must not know), or |rho| > 0.15 with any of the next 5 single-day returns, stage_dc_model refuses to run until it is explained
model: D_C = stage D's exact model (STAGE_D_DECLARATION.json, re-verified) on all 205 clean features PLUS all 123 C features, no selection (D2 showed selection cost information)
decision: compare_d_variants with D as the baseline, identical corrected scoring (ETFs re-drawn out, locked exits moved to the first sellable open): D_C replaces D for a target only if it passes the stage-D gate under that scoring AND its paired daily difference over D has a 98.75% lower bound above zero
conclusion: B (existing features, marginal) vs C (new features, marginal) vs D (all 205, model) vs D2 (B-selected, model) vs D_C (205 + C, model), on corrected scoring, per target
not_in_C: no new target, no honest-exit label (a separate family)
no selection among C features for the model
no outside data beyond the cache (delivery %, sector maps, F&O lists are not available)

B_market_model.name: C_beta_60
B_market_model.formula: OLS slope of the stock's daily log return on m, 60 bars (m = ln(1 + equal-weight mean simple close-to-close return of the universe that day); overnight/intraday analogues from mean simple overnight/intraday returns)
B_market_model.source: Hou & Moskowitz (2005, RFS) price delay; Ang et al. (2006) idiosyncratic volatility; Blitz, Huij & Martens (2011) residual momentum; Blitz et al. (2013, JFM) residual reversal

B_market_model.name: C_beta_down_120
B_market_model.formula: OLS slope on the days with m < 0 within 120 bars
B_market_model.source: Hou & Moskowitz (2005, RFS) price delay; Ang et al. (2006) idiosyncratic volatility; Blitz, Huij & Martens (2011) residual momentum; Blitz et al. (2013, JFM) residual reversal

B_market_model.name: C_beta_updown_120
